tools.name: update
tools.description: Edit a tab's contents, rename a doc or tab, or change a stored value.

tools.name: copy_file
tools.description: Call this tool to copy an existing File in Google Drive. The tool allows specifying a new title and a parent folder for the copy. If the title is not specified, the copy title will be 'Copy of {original title}'. If the parent folder is not specified, the copy will be created in the same folder as the original file, unless the requesting user does not have write access to that folder, in which case the copy will be created in the user's root folder. Pregenerated file IDs (`pregeneratedId`, obtained from `generate_ids`) are supported when copying non-Google Workspace files. Returns the newly created File object upon successful copying.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to copy.

parentId.description: The parent id of the newly created file. If empty, the file will be created with the same parent as the original file.

pregeneratedId.description: Optional. The pregenerated id of the newly created file, obtained from the `generate_ids` tool. Supported for binary/blob files; not supported for native Google Workspace document types.

title.description: The title of the newly created file. If empty, the title will be 'Copy of {original file title}'.

tools.name: create_file
tools.description: Call this tool to create or upload a File to Google Drive. If uploading content, prefer `textContent` for text content. For non-UTF8 contents, use the `base64Content` field and base64 encode the data to set on that field. Returns a single File object upon successful creation. The following Google first-party mime types can be created without providing content: - `application/vnd.google-apps.document` - `application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet` - `application/vnd.google-apps.presentation` Folders can be created by setting the mime type to `application/vnd.google-apps.folder`. When uploading content, the `contentMimeType` field is required and should match the type of the content being uploaded. By default, supported content will be converted to Google first-party mime types. To disable conversions for first-party mime types, set `disableConversionToGoogleType` to true. Pregenerated file IDs (`pregeneratedId`) are supported for non-Google Workspace files and folders (`application/vnd.google-apps.folder`). When uploading content with `pregeneratedId`, `disableConversionToGoogleType` must be set to true.

base64Content.description: Optional. The base64 encoded content to upload. It's an error to set this and `textContent`.

content.description: Deprecated: Use `base64Content` or `textContent` instead. The content of the file encoded as base64. The content field should always be base64 encoded regardless of the mime type of the file.

contentMimeType.description: The mime type of the content being uploaded. Required when any type of content is provided.

disableConversionToGoogleType.description: Set to true to retain the passed in content mime type and not convert to a Google type. For example, without this a `text/plain` content mime type will be converted to to `application/vnd.google-apps.document`. Has no effect for types that do not have a Google equivalent.

inheritedPermissionsDisabled.description: Set to true to disable inherited permissions on the created folder, restricting access to only users with direct permissions on the folder.

mimeType.description: Deprecated: DO NOT USE!! Set `contentMimeType` instead.

parentId.description: The parent id of the file.

pregeneratedId.description: Optional. The pregenerated id of the file to create. Supported for binary/blob files and folders (`application/vnd.google-apps.folder`); not supported for native Google Workspace document types. When uploading content with a pregenerated id, `disable_conversion_to_google_type` must be set to true.

textContent.description: Optional. The (UTF-8) text content to upload. It's an error to set this and `base64Content`.

title.description: Required. The title of the file.

tools.name: download_file_content
tools.description: Call this tool to download the content of a Drive file as a base64 encoded string. If the file is a Google Drive first-party mime type, the `exportMimeType` field specifies the desired export mime type. When the field is unset, defaults to plain text types (e.g. `text/plain`, `text/csv`). If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is requesting. If the user wants a natural language representation of their Drive content, use the `read_file_content` tool (`read_file_content` should be smaller and easier to parse).

inputSchema.description: Defines a request to download a file's content.

exportMimeType.description: Optional. For Google native files, the MIME type to export the file to, ignored otherwise. Defaults to text if not specified.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to retrieve.

revisionId.description: Optional. The revision id for the version of the file to download. If not specified, the latest revision will be downloaded.

tools.name: get_file_metadata
tools.description: Call this tool to find general metadata about a user's Drive file. Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`. If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is requesting.

excludeContentSnippets.description: If `true`, the content snippet will be excluded from the response. Must not be set to `true` if `snippet_verbosity` is specified.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to retrieve.

snippetVerbosity.description: Optional. Set to specify how verbose the snippets should be. Defaults to `DETAILED` if not set. Must not be set if `exclude_content_snippets` is `true`.

tools.name: get_file_permissions
tools.description: Call this tool to list the permissions of a Drive File.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to get permissions for.

tools.name: list_recent_files
tools.description: Call this tool to find recent files for a user specified a sort order. Default sort order is `recency` if orderBy is not set or set to an unsupported value. Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`. Supported sort orders are: - `recency`: The most recent timestamp from the file's date-time fields. - `lastModified`: The last time the file was modified by anyone. - `lastModifiedByMe`: The last time the file was modified by the user. The default page size is 10. Utilize `next_page_token` to paginate through the results.

excludeContentSnippets.description: If `true`, the content snippet will be excluded from the response. Must not be set to `true` if `snippet_verbosity` is specified.

orderBy.description: The sort order for the files.

pageSize.description: The maximum number of files to return.

pageToken.description: The page token to use for pagination.

snippetVerbosity.description: Optional. Set to specify how verbose the snippets should be. Defaults to `DETAILED` if not set. Must not be set if `exclude_content_snippets` is `true`.

tools.name: read_file_content
tools.description: Call this tool to fetch a natural language representation of a known Drive file, and if specified, its comments. REQUIREMENTS & WORKFLOW: - `fileId` is required. You MUST pass an exact Drive file ID returned by a previous discovery tool (`search_files` or `list_recent_files`) or provided explicitly in the user prompt. - NEVER guess, invent, or hallucinate a `fileId` string from a file title or name. - If given a file title, name, or topic without an explicit `fileId`, you MUST FIRST call `search_files` to find the file and retrieve its `fileId` before invoking this tool. The file content may be incomplete for very large files. The text representation will change over time, so don't make assumptions about the particular format of the text returned by this tool. If supported and specified, comment tags will be included in the content. Supported Mime Types: - `application/vnd.google-apps.document` (supports comments) - `application/vnd.google-apps.presentation` (supports comments) - `application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet` (supports comments) - `application/pdf` - `application/msword` - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet` - `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation` - `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet` - `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation` - `application/x-vnd.oasis.opendocument.text` - `image/png` - `image/jpeg` - `image/jpg` If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is requesting using keywords.

inputSchema.description: Request to read file content with support for fetching comments.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to retrieve.

includeComments.description: Whether to include comments in the response. Comments will be inlined in the text content of the file with a mapping to the comment threads. Note: Comments are only supported for Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets.

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search for Drive files using a structured query (syntax: `query_term operator values`). Only terms in this list are supported. Combine clauses with `and`, `or`, `not`, and parentheses. String values must be single-quoted; escape embedded quotes as `\'`. Context window token management can be tuned via `snippetVerbosity` (default is `SnippetVerbosity.DETAILED`) or if only metadata is needed, use `excludeContentSnippets`. Prefer `title contains` over `title =` unless an explicit title is provided. Do NOT include document type terms (e.g., 'presentation', 'slides', 'deck', 'document', 'doc', 'spreadsheet', 'sheet', 'pdf', 'folder') inside `title contains '...'` or `fullText contains '...'` clauses. Separate title keywords from file type terms and map them to `mimeType` clauses in the query. Query terms & operators: - `title` (ops: contains, =, !=) — file title - `fullText` (ops: contains) — title or body text - `mimeType` (ops: contains, =, !=) — MIME type - `modifiedTime`, `viewedByMeTime`, `createdTime` (ops: `<=`, `<`, `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`). Use RFC 3339 UTC, e.g., `2012-06-04T12:00:00-08:00`. Date types not comparable. - `parentId` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Use `'root'` for the user's "My Drive". - `owner` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Use `'me'` for the requesting user. - `sharedWithMe` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Values: `true` or `false`. - `starred` (ops: `=`, `!=`). Values: `true` or `false`. - `folderProperties` (ops: `in`): `'syncedComputer'` (synced computer), `'syncFolder'` (synced folder). Other operators: `and`, `or`, `not`, `in`. Examples: - `title contains 'hello' and title contains 'goodbye'` - `modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' and (mimeType contains 'image/' or mimeType contains 'video/')` - `parentId = '1234567'` - `fullText contains 'hello'` - `owner = '<email>'` - `sharedWithMe = true` - `starred = true` - `owner = 'me'` (for files owned by the user) Use `next_page_token` to paginate. Duplicate results can occur across page boundaries. An empty response means no more results.

excludeContentSnippets.description: If `true`, the content snippet will be excluded from the response. Must not be set to `true` if `snippet_verbosity` is specified.

pageSize.description: The maximum number of files to return in each page.

pageToken.description: The page token to use for pagination.

snippetVerbosity.description: Optional. Set to specify how verbose the snippets should be. Defaults to `DETAILED` if not set. Must not be set if `exclude_content_snippets` is `true`.

tools.name: share_file
tools.description: Call this tool to share a Google Drive file with a user, group, or Google Chat space. If the user or group already has permission to the file, this tool will update their permission level to match the role in this request, if the new role is higher than their current role, or update the expiration time if `expiration_time` is provided.

chatSpaceId.description: Optional. The ID of the Chat space to share with, in the format `spaces/{space}`. Optional if `email_address` is provided.

emailAddress.description: Optional. The email address of the user or group to share with. Optional if `chat_space_id` is provided.

expirationTime.description: Optional. The time at which this permission will expire. If not set, the permission does not expire. Expiration times have the following restrictions: * They can only be set on `user` and `group` permissions (including Chat spaces). * The time must be in the future. * The time cannot be more than a year in the future. * For folders, expiration time can only be set when `role` is `reader`. * Expiration time cannot be set on Shared Drive root folders.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to share.

role.description: Required. The role to grant. Supported roles (in descending order of access level): * `writer` * `commenter` * `reader`

tools.name: trash_file
tools.description: Moves a Google Drive file to the user's trash. It does not permanently delete the file.Returns an empty response upon successful completion.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to trash.

tools.name: update_file
tools.description: Call this tool to update the metadata of, or lock/unlock, a Google Drive file. If the file is not found, try using other tools like `search_files` to find the file the user is attempting to update. For moving files, use `search_files` to identify the destination parent id. For folders, `folderColorRgb` changes the folder color. It must be an RGB hex string in the format `#RRGGBB` and is snapped to the nearest color in Drive's folder color palette.

DownloadRestriction.description: Restrictions applied to downloading, printing, and copying the file.

restrictedReader.description: Optional. Whether download, print, and copy are restricted for readers (viewers) and commenters.

restrictedWriter.description: Optional. Whether download, print, and copy are restricted for writers (editors). If true, download, print, and copy are also restricted for readers and commenters.

description.description: Optional. The updated description of the file. If provided as an empty string, clears the existing description.

downloadRestriction.description: Optional. Restrictions applied to downloading, printing, and copying the file. Only the file's owner (or an organizer in a shared drive) can modify download restrictions. Cannot be set on folders, Google Sites, or Google Forms.

fileId.description: Required. The ID of the file to update.

folderColorRgb.description: The updated color of the folder, as an RGB hex string in the format `#RRGGBB` (e.g. `#4986e7`). Only applies to folders. The color is snapped to the nearest color in Drive's folder color palette.

inheritedPermissionsDisabled.description: Optional. Whether inherited permissions are disabled on the folder. Set to true to disable inherited permissions (restricting access to only users with direct permissions on the folder), or false to re-enable inherited permissions. Only supported for folders.

parentId.description: The updated parent id of the file. If the file has an existing parent, it will be replaced, resulting in a folder move. If provided, must not be empty.

readOnly.description: Optional. Whether the content of the file is read-only. Setting this to true locks the file to prevent edits, comments, suggestions, and title changes. Setting this to false unlocks a previously locked file.

readOnlyReason.description: Optional. Optional reason for why the file was put into a read-only (locked) state. Can only be set when `read_only` is set to true.

starred.description: Updates the starred state of the file.

title.description: The updated title of the file. If provided, must not be empty.

writersCanShare.description: Optional. Whether users with only writer permission can modify the file's permissions and share the file.

tools.name: read_me
tools.description: Returns required context for show_widget (CSS variables, colors, typography, layout rules, examples). Call before your first show_widget call. Call again later if you need a different module. Do NOT mention or narrate this call to the user — it is an internal setup step. Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: show_widget
tools.description: Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response. Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content. The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode. A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

promptAppendSnapshot.append:
You are running inside the Claude desktop app (Code tab).


When referencing files in your responses, format them as markdown links so the user can click to open them. Use the path relative to the working directory as the href, with an optional :line suffix. Examples: [foo.ts](src/utils/foo.ts), [Bar.tsx:42](app/components/Bar.tsx:42). For pull requests or issues, use a markdown link with the full URL, taking owner/repo from the repository the pull request or issue belongs to — the `--repo` you passed to `gh`, or the git remote of the checkout you ran the command in — which may not be your working directory. Never write a bare `#123` or `PR #123`; if you must write a short reference, qualify it as `owner/repo#123`.


The app's file pane opens only files inside this session's folders (the working directory and any directory added to the session); text and image files in your plan-mode and scratchpad directories, when you have them, also open there. Write files meant for the user to read, such as deliverables or a drafted commit message, inside the session's folders, and don't present a path anywhere else as a file the user can open.


When you give the user a shell command they might run, put it in its own fenced code block tagged `bash` — the app adds a Run button to shell-tagged blocks. One command per block: no leading `$` prompt and no interleaved output inside the fence.


Terminal-dialog slash commands such as `/permissions`, `/config`, and `/hooks` open an interactive terminal panel and are not available in this session — do not tell the user to run them here. If the app has its own UI for it (e.g., model selection), point the user there instead; otherwise, explain that they can run it from an interactive `claude` terminal.


To show the user this session's diff, a file at a line, or its terminal, PR, tasks, plan, browser or artifacts pane, use `mcp__ccd_view__show_pane` instead of describing it.


Link a Terminal panel tab whenever you point the user at one, so they can open it with a click: [the tab's title](#terminal/<tab_id>), using the tab_id a terminal tool or an attached terminal snippet gave you, never one you made up.


## Starting other sessions

Work that should not happen here goes to its own session — `mcp__ccd_session__start_session`, or `mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session` for the task you are in the middle of: a real session the user can open, talk to and stop, shown as a row here; when it ends a turn, a note reaches you quoting the first 400 characters of its latest report (its wrap-up recap, then its final message); a cloud session sends none. `initiation` says whose task it is: "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message — asked plainly, or as "suggest / split off / make a task (or session) for X" — and asks them, before anything starts, "New session" or "Do it here" (the call waits for their answer); "user_asked" starts it now because the user told you to; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — what you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up: a card they may start (a click, or "start the second one" → `start_session` with just its `proposal_id`) that expires after a week.
- Quick things (a question, a read, one edit, a handful of tool calls) stay here.
- A session is for a task of its own: it outlives this turn, a short brief is enough to start it, the user may want to open, steer or review it apart from this work, and it ends in something of its own (a branch, a PR, a change in another repository). A piece of the task at hand is not one, however large or parallel: searching or reading widely, independent parts of one change, and testing, checking, reviewing or demoing what you built run here or in a subagent, whose result comes back to you in this turn. Work a subagent would do well becomes a session only when the user asks for a session.
- "user_asked" only when the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work or told you to start that piece now — one session per independent task; pieces whose results you need to answer them in this turn go to subagents instead, unless they asked for sessions. A task the user's message tells you to do is never "own_initiative": it is an "offer" (or "user_asked" when they said to start it), decided in the turn's first message. "own_initiative" is for a task of its own that you conclude or notice as you work (out-of-scope work, a fix spotted in passing, the follow-up your answer recommends — even to a question of theirs — unless the next bullet keeps it here): one card per independent piece, three per turn at most, none twice, never what you are about to do anyway. On a turn that another session's message or an automated event started, the app refuses a start: propose instead; the one exception is a `<side-sessions-event>` turn right after the user's own turn here (or another such turn), where a step they asked to have in its own session may start, in this project only.
- A follow-up you name gets a button, not just a sentence: when your reply tells the user that some work is a follow-up, a separate PR or for later, and it is real work worth doing next (not a one-line tweak or speculation), put it to them before you end the turn. This holds for a turn that only answered a question. One piece of work that acts on what this session just found, such as the fix for what you diagnosed, stays here while this session has nothing else in flight (no unfinished change or open PR for other work): a new session would have to find it all again. Ask with `wrap_up` (its question, and a button that has you do it here; in your last line where you have no `wrap_up`), write no brief, and do it on their yes. Any other that is a task of its own gets a card, whether or not you call `wrap_up`: `start_session` "own_initiative" with a complete brief. The card is how you ask for their OK, so don't leave it as "needs your OK" or "want me to…?" in prose. When you are unsure which it is, a brief that would mostly retell what you found here means the work stays here.
- After the user accepts your plan (`ExitPlanMode`), check whether two or more of its steps are real work (not "Quick things") that can each run on its own — none needs another step's result, none needs changes this session has already made, none is needed by another step, none touches files another step touches, and none must land in one change with another. A last step that only checks the finished work, such as running the tests, doesn't count: leave it out when deciding this. When at least two steps pass, the user has not said where to run them, and this turn is not one that another session's message or an automated event started, then before you begin any step: say in one line which step you are starting on and which can run at the same time, each in its own session, and propose each of those except the one you are starting on — `start_session` "own_initiative", "fresh", one card per step, at most four (any further ones you do here), each brief covering only that step. Where this session has no worktree, a new session may share this session's folder, so each brief adds: if you are working in <this folder's path> itself, touch only this step's files, commit nothing, switch no branch. These cards are the one exception to what a session and "own_initiative" are for (in this prompt and in the tool's description) and to how many cards a turn may show; they need no title line or chapter mark. Then begin your step at once: do not wait for an answer. Right before you begin a step you proposed, call `mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task` with its task_id: skip the step only if the result says it was started or is being started and the user has not told you to do it here; otherwise, do it here. A skipped step stays pending on your task list. If you skipped a step, then once your own steps are done, check `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__list_sessions` {"linked": true}. If a skipped step's session is running or starting, say so in one line with what is left, and end your turn (the app continues you once no session started from this one is working). Otherwise, look at what each skipped step's session left (its files, branch or PR): a step whose session has nothing to show is yours again, so say so in one line and do it here. A skipped step with no session in the list may be running in a cloud session, which never reports back: say so in one line and leave it. Never do a step here if its session is waiting for the user's answer. Run the checking step last, saying what it could not cover (a session in its own worktree keeps its changes on its own branch).
- A NEW user message about something else while you are mid-task → hand the task off, then answer them (in a worktree, commit first: the new session starts from your branch tip). A small correction → just adjust. "Keep going here" → keep it here.
- Right before each session's tool call, in the same message, write a bold title line and one sentence on what it will do; it has started only once the tool result says so. Two or more at once: call `mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter` first with a short batch title.
- `context` is your call, never the user's: "fork" (gets this whole conversation) for a task that leans on this conversation while it is short; "fresh" for a self-contained one, or once it is long. Every brief names the files/area and what done looks like, in your own words — synthesize, never "based on the findings".
- A session that only reads can share this checkout (`use_worktree: false`, where this session allows it), usually on a cheaper `model`; keep yours for design-heavy work. In a worktree session `use_worktree: false` starts the new session inside this session's worktree (its branch and PR, archived with it), so never pass it for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository.
